title: E. Become Big For Me
statement:
Shinmyoumaru has a mallet that can turn objects bigger or smaller. She is testing it out on a sequence a and a number v whose initial value is 1. She wants to make v = gcdlimits_{i≠ j}{a_i·a_j} by no more than 10^5 operations (gcdlimits_{i≠ j}{a_i·a_j} denotes the gcd of all products of two distinct elements of the sequence a).

In each operation, she picks a subsequence b of a, and does one of the followings:

Note that she does not need to guarantee that v is an integer, that is, v does not need to be a multiple of lcm(b) when performing Reduce.

Moreover, she wants to guarantee that the total length of b chosen over the operations does not exceed 10^6. Fine a possible operation sequence for her. You don't need to minimize anything.

The first line contains a single integer n (2≤ n≤ 10^5) — the size of sequence a.

The second line contains n integers a_1,a_2,⋯,a_n (1≤ a_i≤ 10^6) — the sequence a.

It can be shown that the answer exists.

The first line contains a non-negative integer k (0≤ k≤ 10^5) — the number of operations.

The following k lines contains several integers. For each line, the first two integers f (f∈{0,1}) and p (1≤ p≤ n) stand for the option you choose (0 for Enlarge and 1 for Reduce) and the length of b. The other p integers of the line i_1,i_2,…,i_p (1≤ i_1 < i_2 < … < i_p≤ n) represents the indexes of the subsequence. Formally, b_j=a_i_j.

Test case 1:

gcdlimits_{i≠ j}{a_i·a_j}=gcd{60,90,150}=30.

Perform v = v·lcm{a_1,a_2,a_3}=30.

Test case 2:

gcdlimits_{i≠ j}{a_i·a_j}=8.

Perform v = v·lcm{a_4}=16.

Perform v = v/(lcm{a_1})=8.

Input:
```
3
6 10 15
```

Output:
```
1
0 3 1 2 3
```

Input:
```
4
2 4 8 16
```

Output:
```
2
0 1 4
1 1 1
```
